chief_complaint: honey-colored crusted erosions around mouth in child
hpi_details: A 5-year-old girl presents with honey-colored crusted erosions around the mouth that have spread over several days.
ideas: Her mother thinks the sores started as chapped lips from drooling that became infected when she kept touching dirty daycare toys.
concerns: Her mother is worried that the child will be barred from attending preschool orientation and will pass the crusty sores to her six-month-old baby brother.
expectations: Her mother hopes to get an antibiotic ointment and a doctor's clearance note so her daughter can return to preschool on Monday.
social_hx: Lives with family; school attendance to be guided by local infection-control policy

core_concepts: Prompt recognition and structured assessment of Impetigo is essential for guiding targeted diagnostic workup and clinical decision-making.
A thorough clinical history, baseline risk assessment, and targeted objective testing must be synthesized rather than relying on any single symptom in isolation.
Standard management emphasizes Plan for Impetigo Contagiosa: Topical Mupirocin 2% ointment, keep home from school 24h, adapted to individual patient risk factors and clinical severity.
Diagnostic workup and therapeutic decisions should adhere to established clinical guidelines while accounting for patient-specific comorbidities.

Prematurely discharging or reassuring the patient before completing appropriate diagnostic assessment.
Initiating empirical treatment without considering major patient contraindications or drug interactions.

must_ask.say: Does it have a honey-colored crust?
How did it start, and has it spread?
Contact with anyone with a similar rash?

history.answer: Yellowish crusty sores broke out around her mouth a few days ago, and they seem to be spreading.
It started about four days ago as small reddish bumps near the corner of her mouth, and over the past two days they broke open and spread under her nose.
They are only around her mouth and right under her nostrils; there are no rashes on her arms, legs, hands, or feet.
They began as tiny fluid-filled blisters that popped quickly, leaving sticky, honey-colored crusts that look like dried syrup.
She says they itch quite a bit, so she keeps scratching at them, but she doesn't complain of burning or severe pain.
No, they don't fade or come and go like hives; the crusts stay there and gradually get wider as she picks at them.
She has never had anything like this before.
No, she hasn't had any fever, chills, or body aches, and her energy has been normal.
Inside her mouth, gums, and eyes look completely normal, with no sores or redness.
No, her skin is not peeling off in sheets, and there are no dark purple or bruised spots.
Her lips and face aren't swollen, and she is breathing totally fine without any wheezing or tightness.
She hasn't taken any new prescription medications or antibiotics recently.
We haven't changed her soap, lotion, or toothpaste, and she hasn't eaten any new foods or touched strange plants.
One of her classmates at preschool had a similar crusted rash on his face last week, but nobody at home has it yet.
No bug bites, tick exposures, or recent trips to woods, parks, or public swimming pools.
She has never had eczema, asthma, or allergic rhinitis.
No, her joints aren't swollen or painful, and her fingernails look completely normal.
I washed it gently with water and applied some regular petroleum jelly, but I haven't put any antibiotic or steroid cream on it yet.
I thought it was just bad chapped lips or fever blisters from daycare that got infected when she kept picking at them.
I'm terrified she'll pass this nasty crust to her six-month-old brother at home and that preschool will kick her out of orientation.
I was hoping you could give us an antibiotic cream and a doctor's note clearing her to go back to preschool on Monday.
She has always been healthy with no chronic medical conditions.
She has never had surgery and has never been admitted to a hospital.
She does not take any regular medications or supplements.
She has no known allergies to medicines, foods, or latex.
No one smokes in our household or around her.
She is five years old, so there is no alcohol exposure.
She attends a local kindergarten during the day and lives with me, her father, and her three-year-old brother.
There is no family history of psoriasis, eczema, or autoimmune skin diseases.
She was born at full term without any birth complications.
Her growth has been right on track, and all of her routine childhood vaccinations are up to date.

exam.finding: Alert, playful, well-nourished child in no acute distress.
Blood pressure 98/62 mmHg, heart rate 95 beats/min, respiratory rate 20 breaths/min, body temperature 36.8°C, oxygen saturation 99% on room air.

Multiple erythematous erosions with adherent golden honey-colored crusts around the perioral area and under the nose; no active bullae, no induration or warmth extending beyond the crusts, and clear skin elsewhere without involvement of scalp, palms, or soles.
Oral mucosa, tongue, and gingiva are pink and moist without vesicles, aphthae, or erosions; tonsils are not enlarged.
Conjunctivae are clear without injection, discharge, or lesions on the eyelids.
Small, discrete, non-tender submandibular lymph nodes palpable bilaterally; no warm or fluctuant cervical lymphadenopathy.
